sections.h2: How big is Aurora and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Aurora is a home rule city in Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas counties, and it is a principal city of the Denver metro area. It covers about 163.6 square miles, which makes it second in Colorado by land area and roughly 6% larger than Denver.

The 2020 census counted 386,261 residents (336,035 in Arapahoe County, 47,720 in Adams County and 2,506 in Douglas County). The 2025 estimate of 410,053 makes Aurora the third largest city in the state. Because the city touches three counties, your county depends on the address.

Elevation runs from about 5,285 feet near Sand Creek to 6,229 feet at the southern border, nearly a thousand feet of difference across one city.

sections.h2: How did Aurora get its name?
sections.html:
The area was platted around 1890 or 1891 as Fletcher, after Denver businessman Donald Fletcher, and incorporated as the Town of Fletcher on May 5, 1903. It was renamed Aurora in 1907 after one of its subdivisions.

It reincorporated as a city on March 9, 1928, and became one of the fastest growing cities in the country in the late 1970s and early 1980s. That growth explains why so much of its housing is from the 1970s and later.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in Aurora?
sections.html:
Military, health care and schools lead the list. These are figures from the city's reports as summarized on Wikipedia.

Military families and medical staff move often, so Aurora sees sales driven by orders, relocations and new jobs.

sections.h2: What areas and school districts make up Aurora?
sections.html:
Aurora is a patchwork of districts. Aurora Public Schools (Adams-Arapahoe 28J) is the main one, and Cherry Creek Public Schools, Bennett 29-J, School District 27J and Douglas County RE-1 serve other parts.

  • Anschutz Medical Campus, on the former Fitzsimons Army Hospital site
  • Lowry Campus, the former Lowry Air Force Base
  • Downtown A-Town, the historic Fletcher townsite
  • Aurora Highlands, Heather Gardens, Meadowood and Mission Viejo

Part of Stapleton is also inside Aurora. The district on your tax bill and your buyer's school search both depend on the exact address.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and weather shape life in Aurora?
sections.html:
I-70, I-225 and the E-470 beltway cross the city. RTD's H Line serves Dayton and Nine Mile stations, and the R Line reaches Peoria Station, where riders transfer to the A Line to Denver Union Station and Denver International Airport.

The climate is semi-arid, with about 18.2 inches of precipitation a year. July highs average 89 degrees and December lows average 17. Tornado warnings are common between April and July, though the tornadoes are usually weak, so roofs and windows matter to a buyer's inspector.

Aurora has long run an apartment inspection program, and the city council has been weighing a rental registration and licensing program that would cover multifamily and single family rentals. Staff described the idea as yearly registration with a local contact for each rental.

The Sentinel reported that any program would need council approval first. If you own a rental here, check the city's current rules before you list, because registration status can affect a sale.

sections.h2: How does property tax work in Aurora?
sections.html:
Aurora spans three counties, so the bill comes from Arapahoe, Adams or Douglas County, depending on where the house is. The Arapahoe County Treasurer collects tax on the largest share and can be reached at 303-795-4550.

  • A year of revaluation was 2025, and Arapahoe noted that a temporary state exemption used in 2023 and 2024 had expired.
  • Arapahoe lists a senior and military deferral, with applications from January 1 through April 1.
  • The Treasurer takes requests for a Certificate of Taxes Due, used at closing.
  • Residential rates for 2026 are listed as 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.

sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Aurora?
sections.html:
You can list it, sell by owner, or take a cash offer. Cash works well when the house needs repairs, has tenants, or sits in a probate or relocation timeline.

We buy as is. Send your Aurora address and we will tell you how a sale would work, including the tax figures that title will ask for.

faqs.q: How many people live in Aurora?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 410,053, and the 2020 census counted 386,261.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay property tax to in Aurora?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Aurora lies in Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas counties, and most residents are in Arapahoe County.

faqs.q: Does Aurora have a rental license?
faqs.a: The city council has been considering a registration and licensing program for rentals, which would require council approval. Check the city for the current status.

faqs.q: What is the biggest employer in Aurora?
faqs.a: Buckley Space Force Base, with about 12,100 employees in the figures summarized on Wikipedia.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Aurora house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash sale lets you skip repairs, and any unpaid tax is paid from proceeds at closing.
